paper_metadata.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation of Dislocation and Phase Transition for Ni-Based Superalloys with Twist Grain Boundary
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Computational and Theoretical Nanoscience

evidence.quote: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation was carried out to study the dislocation and phase transition of /SLgamma//SLgamma′phase interface for Ni-based superalloys with twist grain boundary (GB) under uniaxial tension.

samples.original_name: Ni/Ni3Al twist GB model, twist angle 1.06°
samples.material_state: relaxed bicrystal with 1.06° twist grain boundary

evidence.quote: The initial orientation of the upper Ni 3Al region (Ni 3Al in L1 2 symmetry) is the same as the lower Ni region (Ni in fcc), and then rotate the upper region around the [001] axis with twist angles of 1.06/compB,3 . 1 0/compB,6 . 3 2/compBand 7.85 /compB.
In modern Ni-based superalloys the /SLgamma′ phase (Ni 3Al) acts as a barrier to dislocation motion.
In modern Ni-based superalloys the /SLgamma′ phase (Ni 3Al) acts as a barrier to dislocation motion.

The geometry of the twist GB system is shown in Figure 1. The crystal is in the cubic orientation (i.e., X-[100], Y -[010], and Z-[001]). The lattice parameters of Ni and Ni 3Al are 3.520 Å and 3.573 Å, respectively.

evidence.quote: The initial orientation of the upper Ni 3Al region (Ni 3Al in L1 2 symmetry) is the same as the lower Ni region (Ni in fcc), and then rotate the upper region around the [001] axis with twist angles of 1.06/compB,3 . 1 0/compB,6 . 3 2/compBand 7.85 /compB.

evidence.quote: The geometry of the twist GB system is shown in Figure 1.
Necking occurs in the middle of the model, as shown in Figure 3. The content of hcp phase is the largest when the twist angle is 6.32 /compB.
Necking occurs in the middle of the model, as shown in Figure 3.

The number of disordered atoms is found at the twist GB when the twist angle is 7.85 /compB. In the mean time, disordered atoms of the other three models are mainly discovered in the necking position.
The conﬁgurations of /SLgamma//SLgamma ′ phase twist GB gradually changes from fcc to hcp judged by CNA, as can be seen in Figure 3.
When strain is above 5.3%, new peaks denotes the appearence of hcp phase. As seen in Figures 4(c) and (d), some peaks have distinct splits when the strain is above 7.5% and 2.5% respectively.

mechanisms.name: dislocation glide
mechanisms.material_state: relaxed bicrystal with 7.85° twist grain boundary

evidence.quote: The reason is that dislocation network is the densest when the twist angle is 7.85 /compB.T h e dislocation network reduces the ability of resistance to dislocation glide.
The fcc-to-hcp phase transition was observed during the uniaxial tensile process.

mechanisms.name: lattice expansion along [001] and compression along [100]/[010]

evidence.quote: The lattices constant are expanded in the tensile direction of [001], and the lattices are compressed to a certain extent in the directions of [100] and [010]. Consequently, the lattice constant of fcc phase is changed into the lattice constant of hcp phase.
